notes: Observations: Final twist: S (0-33.0), Z (33.0 - 59.5), S (59.5 - 83.0) 1) The pendant cords are all (w/exception of last two) attached to the primary cord by an overhand knot made with the twisted end of the pendant around the primary cord. After knotting, the twisted end was cut off at teh top of the knot, along the top edge of the primary cord. This gives the top edge of the primary cord. This gives the top edge of the primary cord a "tufted" appearance. In the table, knot attachment is identified as "O" (overhand). Diagrams attached. 2) A cord has been carried around primary cord on top of attachment knots of pendants #3-5. This cord, which may have formed a loop (e.g. for suspending the khipus) is broken. 3) Pendant 119 contains a subsidiar knotted and wrapped six turns around pendant cord. Diagram attached.
